masonry.value: No enforceable masonry percentage for new single-family homes made of materials approved by a national model code (Gov't Code ch. 3000, HB 2439, 2019); exceptions: designated historic districts/landmarks, and windstorm/flood-insurance materials. Older city masonry percentages for single-family homes cannot be enforced against code-approved materials, except in historic districts.

source.title: HB 2439 (2019) staff summary - Fort Worth Development Services (Gov't Code ch. 3000 building-materials preemption)

plainLanguage: Arlington is a large North Texas city that most likely builds homes under the 2021 International Residential Code with the regional NCTCOG amendments; this has not been confirmed yet. North Texas clay soils swell and shrink, so plan on an engineer-designed post-tensioned slab foundation. Your lot's zoning district and subdivision plat set how far the house must sit from the property lines. We have not verified those numbers for Arlington yet, so enter them from your plat or zoning letter. State law stops the city from requiring a brick or stone percentage on a normal lot, but your HOA or deed restrictions may still require one. Arlington is believed to charge water and wastewater impact fees on new homes. Permit, impact and tap fees still need to be confirmed with the city.
